articles.title: Rupee scales 8-month high after holiday as foreign flows to Indian equities persist
articles.content: The Indian rupee has shown significant strength against the US dollar, propelled by robust foreign portfolio investments. Surging to an eight-month high on Thursday, it closed at 92.23 per dollar. Analysts connect this to favorable market dynamics, including falling crude oil prices. With record foreign investments in Indian stocks this month, the market exudes increased confidence, suggesting a potential for continued rupee appreciation if circumstances remain favorable.

India pension funds pivot to bonds as equity exposure nears cap
articles.content: As India’s largest pension funds edge closer to the equity caps, a strategic pivot towards government bonds has been observed. UTI Pension Fund is channeling 50% of its new investments into government bonds, a marked increase from last year, while SBI Pension Funds aims to cut stock allocations to just 25%. This shift comes as markets rally, and a heightened bond focus could bolster India's debt market significantly.

articles.content: The US dollar remained steady as traders awaited important inflation and growth data prior to December. In Japan, service-sector prices surged to a 36-year high, while the Australian dollar rose after inflation data exceeded forecasts. Concerns about the sustainability of the AI market have impacted investor sentiment.

articles.title: Goldman Sachs, SocGen buy Rs 920 crore stake in Lenskart
articles.content: Goldman Sachs and Societe Generale have jointly invested ₹920 crore to purchase a 1% stake in Lenskart Solutions, acquiring 65.21 lakh and 61.76 lakh shares priced at ₹725 each. Steadview Capital Management facilitated this by selling an equivalent number of shares, resulting in their stake decreasing from 3.31% to 2.58%. Following this, Lenskart’s stock slid approximately 4%, ending the day at ₹715.90.

articles.title: PE/VC investments in India surge to USD 8.7 billion in October, highest monthly level in five years: EY-IVCA report
articles.content: Private equity and venture capital investments in India surged to USD 8.7 billion in October 2026. This monthly figure is the highest recorded in the past five years, supported by eight large deals totaling USD 7.3 billion. Financial services attracted the majority of investments, amounting to USD 5.9 billion during this period. Despite the increase in investments, exit activity declined, with 21 exits valued at USD 544 million.

Shift in pension and insurance money to equities dampens long-term G-sec demand: RBI DG
articles.content: The demand for long-term government securities has seen a marginal decline recently. Insurance companies and pension funds are increasingly focusing on equities instead of sovereign debt. This change has impacted the stability of the government securities market and highlighted challenges in liquidity distribution. The Reserve Bank of India emphasizes the need for a coordinated approach and broader participation from institutional investors.
